statements.subject: English
statements.text: drawing on new vocabulary and grammatical constructions from their reading and listening, and using these consciously in their writing and speech to achieve particular effects

statements.subject: English
statements.text: knowing and understanding the differences between spoken and written language, including differences associated with formal and informal registers, and between Standard English and other varieties of English

statements.subject: English
statements.text: using Standard English confidently in their own writing and speech

statements.subject: English
statements.text: discussing reading, writing and spoken language with precise and confident use of linguistic and literary terminology*

statements.subject: English
statements.text: speak confidently and effectively, including through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: using Standard English confidently in a range of formal and informal contexts, including classroom discussion

statements.subject: English
statements.text: giving short speeches and presentations, expressing their own ideas and keeping to the point

statements.subject: English
statements.text: participating in formal debates and structured discussions, summarising and/or building on what has been said

statements.subject: English
statements.text: improvising, rehearsing and performing play scripts and poetry in order to generate languages and discuss language use and meaning, using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness and action to add impact

statements.subject: English
statements.text: read and appreciate the depth and power of the English literary heritage through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: reading a wide range of high-quality, challenging, classic literature and extended literary non-fiction, such as essays, reviews and journalism. This writing should include whole texts. The range will include:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: at least one play by Shakespeare

statements.subject: English
statements.text: works from the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries

statements.subject: English
statements.text: poetry since 1789, including representative Romantic poetry

statements.subject: English
statements.text: re-reading literature and other writing as a basis for making comparisons

statements.subject: English
statements.text: choosing and reading books independently for challenge, interest and enjoyment

statements.subject: English
statements.text: understand and critically evaluate texts through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: reading in different ways for different purposes, summarising and synthesising ideas and information, and evaluating their usefulness for particular purposes

statements.subject: English
statements.text: drawing on knowledge of the purpose, audience for and context of the writing, including its social, historical and cultural context and the literary tradition to which it belongs, to inform evaluation

statements.subject: English
statements.text: identifying and interpreting themes, ideas and information

statements.subject: English
statements.text: exploring aspects of plot, characterisation, events and settings, the relationships between them and their effects

statements.subject: English
statements.text: seeking evidence in the text to support a point of view, including justifying inferences with evidence

statements.subject: English
statements.text: distinguishing between statements that are supported by evidence and those that are not, and identifying bias and misuse of evidence

statements.subject: English
statements.text: analysing a writer’s choice of vocabulary, form, grammatical and structural features, and evaluating their effectiveness and impact

statements.subject: English
statements.text: making critical comparisons, referring to the contexts, themes, characterisation, style and literary quality of texts, and drawing on knowledge and skills from wider reading

statements.subject: English
statements.text: make an informed personal response, recognising that other responses to a text are possible and evaluating these

statements.subject: English
statements.text: write accurately, fluently, effectively and at length for pleasure and information through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: adapting their writing for a wide range of purposes and audiences: to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, give and respond to information, and argue

statements.subject: English
statements.text: selecting and organising ideas, facts and key points, and citing evidence, details and quotation effectively and pertinently for support and emphasis

statements.subject: English
statements.text: selecting, and using judiciously, vocabulary, grammar, form, and structural and organisational features, including rhetorical devices, to reflect audience, purpose and context, and using Standard English where appropriate

statements.subject: English
statements.text: make notes, draft and write, including using information provided by others [e.g. writing a letter from key points provided; drawing on and using information from a presentation]

statements.subject: English
statements.text: revise, edit and proof-read through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: reflecting on whether their draft achieves the intended impact

statements.subject: English
statements.text: restructuring their writing, and amending its grammar and vocabulary to improve coherence, consistency, clarity and overall effectiveness

statements.subject: English
statements.text: paying attention to the accuracy and effectiveness of grammar, punctuation and spelling

statements.subject: English
statements.text: consolidate and build on their knowledge of grammar and vocabulary through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: studying their effectiveness and impact in the texts they read

statements.subject: English
statements.text: drawing on new vocabulary and grammatical constructions from their reading and listening, and using these consciously in their writing and speech to achieve particular effects

statements.subject: English
statements.text: analysing some of the differences between spoken and written language, including differences associated with formal and informal registers, and between Standard English and other varieties of English

statements.subject: English
statements.text: using linguistic and literary terminology accurately and confidently in discussing reading, writing and spoken language

statements.subject: English
statements.text: speak confidently, audibly and effectively, including through:

statements.subject: English
statements.text: using Standard English when the context and audience require it

statements.subject: English
statements.text: working effectively in groups of different sizes and taking on required roles, including leading and managing discussions, involving others productively, reviewing and summarising, and contributing to meeting goals/deadlines

statements.subject: English
statements.text: listening to and building on the contributions of others, asking questions to clarify and inform, and challenging courteously when necessary

statements.subject: English
statements.text: planning for different purposes and audiences, including selecting and organising information and ideas effectively and persuasively for formal spoken presentations and debates

statements.subject: English
statements.text: listening and responding in a variety of different contexts, both formal and informal, and evaluating content, viewpoints, evidence and aspects of presentation

statements.subject: English
statements.text: improvising, rehearsing and performing play scripts and poetry in order to generate language and discuss language use and meaning, using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness and action to add impact
